idiom_name: createSlice with PayloadAction<T>, inferred RootState, typed hooks
implementation_notes: TypeScript is Redux Toolkit's first-class environment: createSlice infers the reducer, the action creators and the PayloadAction<T> type from the reducers you write, configureStore infers RootState and a typed AppDispatch, and the documented useAppSelector/useAppDispatch hooks carry those types into components, so dispatching the wrong payload fails to compile. Selectors are typed functions over RootState, createAsyncThunk types the fulfilled/rejected payloads, and Immer keeps the mutable-looking reducers safe. A hand-written discriminated-union action type with a plain reducer remains the dependency-free baseline when the store is trivial; the toolkit route is justified as soon as more than a couple of features share the state.
pitfalls: Widening the state type (any, a non-null assertion on state.todos) erases the inference that makes the slice safe; keep the inferred types and export them.
A selector typed (state: any) accepts any store and silently returns undefined on a rename; type selectors on RootState.
Action payloads typed as a mutable object can be mutated by middleware after dispatch; treat payloads as readonly and copy on the way in.
createAsyncThunk error typing is easy to widen to unknown-any: declare the rejected value type or the error branch loses its shape at the call site.

variants.name: NgRx Store for Angular (createAction / createReducer, DI-provided)
variants.idiom_name: createAction + props<T>(), createReducer + on(), typed selectors and effects
variants.implementation_notes: NgRx is the Redux implementation of the Angular ecosystem: createAction('[Todos] Add', props<{ text: string }>()) builds typed, memoised action creators, createReducer/on compose pure reducer functions per feature slice, and the store is provided through dependency injection with select() and createSelector for typed reads, while @ngrx/effects handle asynchronous work and dispatch further actions. The state model is exactly Redux's; what differs from the toolkit route is the DI wiring, the effects/entity ecosystem and Angular's release-train version coupling, which is why the same reducer logic looks different at the call site.
pitfalls: Registering the same feature twice (StoreModule.forFeature/forRoot in two lazy routes) silently duplicates the state branch; keep registration in one place.
Reducers run under runtime immutability checks in development, so an accidental mutation throws there and lies to selectors in production builds.
An effect that dispatches its own triggering action loops indefinitely; gate it with distinctUntilChanged or takeUntil on an action type that ends the cycle.
